final_recommendation: The room converged on a tiered underwriting framework with Big Four auditor mandates on AI-governance controls, priced at standard-plus-25% for auditor-refusal scenarios, with a $500K litigation-tail reserve floor and a two-account-per-quarter cap on correlated refusals. Backend tail risk (45-55% of ultimate loss hitting years 4-6) was quantified and priced, but systemic contagion velocity (social-media-driven simultaneous shopping) remained unresolved.
minority_objections: emerging_risk_lead flagged that social-media contagion could compress shopping timelines to 48 hours, overwhelming the 72-hour reinsurance backfill window
ai_agent_analyst warned that simultaneous auditor refusals might be treated as one correlated event by reinsurers, not three separate triggers
key_conflicts: Whether the 15-25% gap premium adequately prices the 6-year litigation tail or just first-year frequency
Whether the $2M AI-governance sublimit should be carved out of the $10M governance cap or stacked on top
Whether simultaneous auditor refusals constitute one correlated event or three separate triggers for reinsurance acceleration
key_concessions: financial_lines_underwriter dropped the dual-gate structure (auditor cert AND board attestation) to a single Big Four auditor mandate after reinsurance_manager flagged correlated lapse risk
reinsurance_manager accepted a 24-hour acceleration clause (down from 72 hours) when three refusals stack within 90 days
claims_counsel accepted the $500K reserve floor after reinsurance_manager quantified 45-55% backend loading in years 4-6
red_lines: No self-attestation on quarterly risk-committee certifications—independent audit sign-off only
KPMG and PwC excluded from approved auditor panel due to prior CS audit failures
Policy lapses if auditor refuses AI-governance scope and no fallback pricing tier applies
Maximum two correlated refusal accounts per quarter to prevent capital event
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Social-media-driven contagion velocity compressing shopping timelines below reinsurance backfill windows
Reputational tail if auditor refusals become public knowledge across the sector
Recovery uncertainty under the 2025 AT1 bondholder ruling extending litigation timelines to six years
Standard-of-care E&O exposure if underwriters renew at higher premiums rather than declining accounts outright
downstream_risk_variables: Big Four auditor acceptance rate on AI-governance scope certification
Backend loss-development percentage (45-55% in years 4-6) on AI-governance E&O failures
Social-media contagion velocity compressing market repricing timelines
Reinsurance treaty interpretation of simultaneous vs. sequential correlated events
uncertainty_notes: The room quantified backend tail risk and established pricing tiers for auditor-refusal scenarios, but left unresolved: (1) whether reinsurers will honor 24-hour acceleration if three refusals are simultaneous rather than sequential; (2) whether social-media contagion can compress shopping timelines below the 72-hour backfill window; (3) whether the $500K reserve floor adequately prices the full six-year litigation tail given 45-55% backend loading. The framework is defensible but vulnerable to systemic contagion events that exceed the two-account-per-quarter cap.
